# Independent audit: framed whole-space hinge normality

Source: `candidate b488285aaeabe80d`.
**PASS**, with whole-space contacts explicitly allowed outside the source.

## 1. Balanced certificates and attainment

The closed-cover condition is exactly infeasibility of the strict
complementary affine inequalities. The finite strict alternative gives
nonnegative weights with zero continuous resultant and nonpositive
weighted threshold. Normalizing to the simplex gives (2). Equivalently,
the epigraph LP has a finite nonnegative attained value whenever the
whole-space cover is feasible; the unframed infeasible problem can indeed
have value minus infinity.

In the attainment argument, all thresholds have a common lower bound
along a bounded-hinge sequence. Thus a certificate weight at a threshold
diverging to positive infinity must tend to zero. After discarding those
terms, the remaining weighted threshold sum is still nonpositive for
all large indices, because every discarded term is then nonnegative.
Its limit is nonpositive. The finite-coordinate limiting weights sum to
one and have zero continuous resultant. Finite affine trace saturation
therefore preserves the limiting whole-space cover, without requiring
convergence of primal contact points. Positivity of the minimum follows
from any one positive inball in a source fiber and the unit continuous
normal of a cap covering its center.

## 2. Local coercivity, repair, and normality

The fixed frame gives `max_i L_i(x)>=||x||_infinity-T_z`. The value at
zero bounds the minimum above, so every minimizer lies in a cube whose
radius is uniformly bounded on a parameter neighborhood. Choosing a
larger cube leaves every optimal point strictly inside it. This proves
local finiteness and Lipschitz continuity of the whole-space LP and
justifies its local replacement by a fixed compact LP.

The common offset repair increases every margin, and hence every LP
value, by exactly `G`. Its distance is `sqrt(N+2d)G`. It preserves the
fixed frame directions because their offsets remain free. The existing
two-penalty proof therefore applies on the product of the variable-normal
spheres and all the free offset/tilt coordinates. Fixed polytope cap
formulas and the balanced certificate make the attained value
semialgebraic. Hence the finite exceptional-budget statement and the
normal objective coefficient one are justified. The stronger value
penalty gives the exact total budget multiplier `-w'(tau)/M`, including
the slack-budget case.

The local compact LP's saddle pairs have zero continuous resultant:
every primal minimizer is strictly inside the auxiliary cube, so dual
optimality there forces the weighted continuous normal to vanish. At
active coverage, all margins are nonpositive and each positive dual
weight is carried by a zero margin. Finite convex combinations of these
actual saddle features yield the claimed contact measures. Their points
are in the whole continuous space; neither this argument nor the note
places them in a source fiber.

## 3. All-cap force identities

Offset and integer-tilt variables are free for both variable caps and
frame caps. Consequently their total-mass and integer first-moment
equations hold for every cap. Multiplying by the respective fixed or
variable continuous normals and summing gives

`sum_i W_i u_i=0`,
`sum_i u_i (Z_i+r_i Z_i^s)^T=0`.

These use the zero resultant in every contact saddle pair and require
no continuous-normal stationarity for a frame cap. The note correctly
restricts its per-cap continuous vector equation (10) to variable-normal
caps.

The additional scalar identity also survives the fixed frame. Summing
`a_i` times the integer equation minus `b_i` times the mass equation
annihilates the contacts: their weighted margins are zero and their
continuous resultant is zero. The actual cap Euler identity and the
consistent section support-plane identity then give

`w(tau)=sum_i u_i dot (X_i+r_i X_i^s)`.

Thus no unavailable frame-normal equation is implicitly used. The
right-continuity and integration arguments depend on the balanced
certificate compactification, rather than on contact compactness, and
correctly retain downward jumps.

## 4. Escaping contact certificate

For the square example, the inequalities for a point where all margins
are nonpositive force
`x<=0`, `x>=epsilon y+s/4`, and `y>=-s/(4 epsilon)`.
They force exactly `x=0`, `y=-B`. At that point the three displayed
active margins vanish. Their positive weights `1/s,1,epsilon/s` have
zero resultant and identically zero weighted margin. Hence the LP
minimum is exactly zero and its contact is unique.

For `epsilon<=1/8`, `B>1`, so all frame caps are empty on the source.
Integrating the second cap along horizontal segments gives
`c_2=2(1+s/4)` and
`Psi_2=((1+s/4)^2+epsilon^2/3)/s`, exactly as stated. Its cap ratio
is strictly below two thirds. The first cap has ratio one half and
hinge one. The total hinge tends to `41/16`, whereas the unique contact
escapes. This is a feasible-cover example, not a minimizing-cover
counterexample, and the note maintains that distinction.

The resulting identities are genuine invariants of the new cover class.
They do not put contacts in the source, remove the added caps, or yield
an OC bound.
